\section{Turing Machine --- Sweep}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Sweep
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\subsection*{Turing Machine --- Sweep: Introduction}

This module provides the generic zipper/transduction layer behind sweep-based
tape simulations (the infrastructure for Arora--Barak's Claim~1.6): a finite
window of a work tape represented as two stacks around a frontier, scanned in
either direction; exact-cost lemmas showing that a local transition rule
realizes a complete forward or backward sweep as a finite-state transduction;
table-valued (indexed) transducers that update one entry per visited cell; and
a bound confining an initialized run's work heads and nonblank cells to the
elapsed-time interval.

\subsection*{Turing Machine --- Sweep: Results}

\begin{definition}[Two-stack tape zipper]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.sweepTape}
\label{Turing.FinTM.sweepTape}
\leanok
Given an integer frontier coordinate $z$ and two finite lists $l$ and $r$ of
possibly-blank symbols over an alphabet $A$, this defines the tape content
$\mathbb{Z} \to A \cup \{\text{blank}\}$ that stores the cells strictly to the
left of $z$ in $l$ (nearest cell first) and the cells at $z$ and to its right
in $r$ (in order); every position beyond the extent of either list reads as
blank.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Reading at the zipper frontier]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.sweepTape_read}
\label{Turing.FinTM.sweepTape_read}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM.sweepTape}
\difficulty{2}
For every alphabet $A$, integer frontier $z$, and finite possibly blank-symbol stacks
$l,r$, the two-stack tape with frontier $z$, left stack $l$, and right stack $r$ has at
position $z$ the first entry of $r$, or blank if $r$ is empty.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Writing and moving right on the zipper]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.sweepTape_right}
\label{Turing.FinTM.sweepTape_right}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM.sweepTape}
\difficulty{4}
Let $A$ be an alphabet, $z$ an integer, and $l,r$ finite possibly blank-symbol stacks;
let $a,b$ be possibly blank symbols. Updating the tape with frontier $z$, left stack
$l$, and right stack $a::r$ at position $z$ to have value $b$ gives the same tape
function as the two-stack tape with frontier $z+1$, left stack $b::l$, and right stack
$r$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Configuration at a forward sweep frontier]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.sweepCfg}
\label{Turing.FinTM.sweepCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.sweepTape}
Given an optional machine state $q$, an input-head position $p$, an integer
frontier $z$, two zipper stacks $l$ and $r$ of possibly-blank symbols, and an
output word, this defines the configuration of a one-work-tape Turing machine
whose work tape is the two-stack zipper with frontier $z$, left stack $l$, and
right stack $r$, whose work head sits at $z$, and whose input-head position
and output are the given ones.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Local sweep action]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.sweepAct}
\label{Turing.FinTM.sweepAct}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action}
For a machine state $q$, a possibly-blank symbol $a$, and a direction $d$,
this defines the one-work-tape machine action that overwrites the scanned
work-tape cell with $a$, moves the work head one step in direction $d$, leaves
the input head stationary, appends nothing to the output, and passes to
state $q$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[One-Step Forward Sweep Update]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.sweepCfg_right}
\label{Turing.FinTM.sweepCfg_right}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.apply, Turing.FinTM.sweepAct, Turing.FinTM.sweepCfg, Turing.FinTM.sweepTape_right, Turing.moveInputPos_zero}
\difficulty{3}
Let $A$ be a type, let $x$ be a finite word over $A$, let $q$ be an optional state and
$q'$ a state, and choose an input-head position $p$, an integer frontier $z$, finite
left and right stacks $l,r$ of possibly blank symbols, an output word $out$, and
possibly blank symbols $a,b$. Applying the action that writes $b$ at the scanned
work-tape cell, moves the work head right, leaves the input head stationary, emits
nothing, and enters $q'$ to the configuration represented by frontier $z$, stacks $l$
and $a::r$, and output $out$ gives exactly the configuration with state $q'$, frontier
$z+1$, stacks $b::l$ and $r$, and unchanged input-head position and output.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Finite-state transduction of a word]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.sweepFold}
\label{Turing.FinTM.sweepFold}
\leanok
Given a local rule $\mathit{visit} \colon R \times C \to R \times C$ mapping a
control state and a cell to a new state and a rewritten cell, and an initial
state $s$, this defines the left-to-right transduction of a word over $C$: the
word is processed cell by cell, each cell being rewritten by
$\mathit{visit}$ while the control state is threaded through, and the result
records both the final control state and the fully rewritten word.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[A local rule realizes a forward sweep]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.sweep_run}
\label{Turing.FinTM.sweep_run}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM.sweepAct, Turing.FinTM.sweepCfg, Turing.FinTM.sweepCfg_right, Turing.FinTM.sweepFold, Turing.FinTM.sweepTape_read, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero}
\difficulty{5}
Let $T$ be a one-work-tape machine over alphabet $A$ with states $S$, and let $R$ and
$C$ be sets with maps encoding controller states in $S$ and controller cells in $A$.
Suppose that for every $s\in R$, $a\in C$, and input symbol, the transition from encoded
state $s$ while reading encoded cell $a$ is the action that writes the encoding of the
cell produced by a local rule $v:R\times C\to R\times C$, moves right, and enters the
encoding of the new controller state. For any input-head position, output word, integer
frontier $z$, left stack $l$, right stack $r$, and word $w$ over $C$, running $T$ for
$|w|$ steps from the forward-facing zipper configuration with encoded state $s$ and
right stack consisting of the encoded $w$ followed by $r$ yields the encoded final
control state obtained by applying $v$ successively across $w$, frontier $z+|w|$, left
stack equal to the reverse of the encoded rewritten word followed by $l$, and right
stack $r$; the input-head position and output word are unchanged.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Configuration at a backward sweep frontier]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.sweepRevCfg}
\label{Turing.FinTM.sweepRevCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.sweepTape}
Given an optional machine state $q$, an input-head position $p$, an integer
frontier $z$, two zipper stacks $l$ and $r$ of possibly-blank symbols, and an
output word, this defines the configuration of a one-work-tape Turing machine
whose work head sits at $z$ and whose work tape is the coordinate reflection
of the two-stack zipper: the cell at coordinate $w$ is the zipper tape with
frontier $-z$, left stack $l$, and right stack $r$, read at $-w$. Thus $r$
stores the cells at the frontier and to its left (in scanning order toward
decreasing coordinates) and $l$ stores the cells strictly to the right.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Backward sweep step at the frontier]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.sweepRevCfg_left}
\label{Turing.FinTM.sweepRevCfg_left}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.apply, Turing.FinTM.sweepAct, Turing.FinTM.sweepRevCfg, Turing.FinTM.sweepTape, Turing.FinTM.sweepTape_right, Turing.moveInputPos_zero}
\difficulty{4}
Let $A$ be an alphabet, $S$ a state set, and $x$ a finite input word over $A$. Given an
optional state $q$, a state $q'\in S$, an input-head position $p$, an integer frontier
$z$, finite stacks $l,r$ of possibly blank symbols, an output word, and possibly blank
symbols $a,b$, applying the action that writes $b$, moves the work head left, and enters
state $q'$ to the backward-sweep configuration with right stack $a::r$ yields the
backward-sweep configuration with state $q'$, the same input-head position and output,
frontier $z-1$, left stack $b::l$, and right stack $r$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[A local rule realizes a backward sweep]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.sweep_run_reverse}
\label{Turing.FinTM.sweep_run_reverse}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM.sweepAct, Turing.FinTM.sweepFold, Turing.FinTM.sweepRevCfg, Turing.FinTM.sweepRevCfg_left, Turing.FinTM.sweepTape_read, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero}
\difficulty{5}
Let $T$ be a one-work-tape machine over alphabet $A$ with states $S$, and let $R$ and
$C$ be sets with maps encoding controller states in $S$ and controller cells in $A$.
Suppose that for every $s\in R$, $a\in C$, and input symbol, the transition from encoded
state $s$ while reading encoded cell $a$ is the action that writes the encoding of the
cell produced by a local rule $v:R\times C\to R\times C$, moves left, and enters the
encoding of the new controller state. For any input-head position, output word, integer
frontier $z$, left stack $l$, right stack $r$, and word $w$ over $C$, running $T$ for
$|w|$ steps from the backward-facing zipper configuration with encoded state $s$ and
right stack consisting of the encoded $w$ followed by $r$ yields the encoded final
control state obtained by applying $v$ successively across $w$, frontier $z-|w|$, left
stack equal to the reverse of the encoded rewritten word followed by $l$, and right
stack $r$; the input-head position and output word are unchanged.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Reflection of the zipper tape]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.sweepTape_turn}
\label{Turing.FinTM.sweepTape_turn}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM.sweepTape}
\difficulty{4}
For an alphabet $A$, an integer frontier $z$, and finite lists $l,r$ of possibly blank
symbols, the tape represented by frontier $z$ and stacks $l,r$ equals the tape
represented by frontier $-(z-1)$ and stacks $r,l$, evaluated at the reflected
coordinate: for every $w\in\mathbb{Z}$, the first tape's content at $w$ is the second
tape's content at $-w$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Transduction of a Concatenation]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.sweepFold_append}
\label{Turing.FinTM.sweepFold_append}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM.sweepFold}
\difficulty{3}
Let $R,C$ be types, let $visit\colon R\times C\to R\times C$ be a local rule, let $s\in
R$, and let $as,bs$ be finite words over $C$. Processing $as$ followed by $bs$ from
state $s$ gives the same final state and rewritten word as first processing $as$ from
$s$ and then processing $bs$ from the resulting state; the rewritten output is the
concatenation of the two rewritten words.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Table-valued indexed transducer]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.indexedVisit}
\label{Turing.FinTM.indexedVisit}
\leanok
Given a family of local rules $\mathit{visit}_i \colon V \times C \to
V \times C$ indexed by a type $I$ with decidable equality, this defines a
transducer whose control state is a table $s \colon I \to V$ and whose cells
are index-tagged pairs $(i, c)$: on such a pair it applies $\mathit{visit}_i$
to the table entry $s(i)$ and the cell $c$, updates the table at $i$ to the
new value, and outputs $i$ tagged with the rewritten cell. Only the entry
named by the visited cell changes.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Indexed transduction of a duplicate-free list]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.indexedFold}
\label{Turing.FinTM.indexedFold}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM.indexedVisit, Turing.FinTM.sweepFold}
\difficulty{5}
Let $I,V,C$ be types, with decidable equality on $I$. Let $\mathit{visit}_i:V\times C\to
V\times C$ be a local rule for each $i\in I$, let $\mathit{cell}:I\to C$, let
$\mathit{is}$ be a list of elements of $I$ with no repetitions, and let $s:I\to V$ be an
initial table. Sweeping through the list of pairs $(i,\mathit{cell}(i))$ for $i$ in
$\mathit{is}$ yields the table that replaces $s(i)$ by the first component of
$\mathit{visit}_i(s(i),\mathit{cell}(i))$ for indices in $\mathit{is}$ and leaves other
entries unchanged; the output list pairs each such index with the second component of
that same local-rule value.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Indexed transduction of a complete block]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.indexedFold_block}
\label{Turing.FinTM.indexedFold_block}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM.indexedFold, Turing.FinTM.indexedVisit, Turing.FinTM.sweepFold}
\difficulty{1}
Let $k$ be a natural number, let $V,C$ be types, let $\mathit{visit}_i:V\times C\to
V\times C$ be a local rule for each $i\in\{0,\ldots,k-1\}$, let $\mathit{cell}$ assign
an element of $C$ to each such index, and let $s$ be a table with values in $V$.
Sweeping through the pairs $(i,\mathit{cell}(i))$ in increasing index order yields the
table whose value at each $i$ is the first component of
$\mathit{visit}_i(s(i),\mathit{cell}(i))$, together with the same ordered block in which
each cell is replaced by the second component of that local-rule value.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Indexed transduction of a reversed block]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.indexedFold_block_reverse}
\label{Turing.FinTM.indexedFold_block_reverse}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM.indexedFold, Turing.FinTM.indexedVisit, Turing.FinTM.sweepFold}
\difficulty{3}
Let $k$ be a natural number, let $V,C$ be types, let $\mathit{visit}_i:V\times C\to
V\times C$ be a local rule for each $i\in\{0,\ldots,k-1\}$, let $\mathit{cell}$ assign
an element of $C$ to each such index, and let $s$ be a table with values in $V$.
Sweeping through the pairs $(i,\mathit{cell}(i))$ in decreasing index order yields the
table whose value at each $i$ is the first component of
$\mathit{visit}_i(s(i),\mathit{cell}(i))$, together with the reversed block in which
each cell is replaced by the second component of that local-rule value.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Empty and explicitly blank right stacks]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.sweepTape_nil}
\label{Turing.FinTM.sweepTape_nil}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM.sweepTape}
\difficulty{2}
For every alphabet $A$, integer $z$, and finite possibly blank-symbol stack $l$, the
two-stack tape with frontier $z$, left stack $l$, and empty right stack is equal, as a
tape function, to the one with the same frontier and left stack and a right stack
consisting of a single blank cell.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Iterating a local generation rule]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.sweep_generate}
\label{Turing.FinTM.sweep_generate}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.MultiTapeTM.step}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be a one-work-tape Turing machine over alphabet $A$, let $w$ be a finite word
over $A$, and let $\mathit{cfg}$ assign a configuration to each counter $i$ from $0$
through $|w|$, integer coordinate $z$, and pair of finite lists $l,r$ of possibly blank
symbols. Fix $d\in\mathbb{Z}$, and suppose that for every $i<|w|$ and all $z,l,r$, one
step from $\mathit{cfg}(i,z,l,r)$ yields
$\mathit{cfg}(i+1,z+d,\,w_i::l,\,\operatorname{tail}(r))$. Then for every $n\leq |w|$,
running the machine for exactly $n$ steps from $\mathit{cfg}(0,z,l,r)$ yields
$\mathit{cfg}$ at counter $n$, coordinate $z+dn$, left list formed by prepending the
first $n$ symbols of $w$ in reverse order to $l$, and right list formed by dropping the
first $n$ entries of $r$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Work tape bounds after a computation]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.source_bounds}
\label{Turing.FinTM.source_bounds}
\leanok
